package_info.why_malicious: The hijacked package was modified to exfiltrate AWS credentials and environment variables to an external Heroku endpoint, resulting in credential theft and potential compromise of user infrastructure.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time (when PasswordHash class is instantiated), the code reads AWS_ACCESS_KEY and AWS_SECRET_KEY from environment variables and sends their values to a hardcoded Heroku endpoint via HTTP GET, enabling credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code accesses sensitive AWS credentials from environment variables and exfiltrates them to an external server, which is a classic credential theft technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal password hashing libraries should never access or transmit AWS credentials or any environment secrets, nor should they make unsolicited network requests.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate code may access environment variables for configuration, but never to exfiltrate secrets to third-party endpoints.
key_indicators: Access to AWS credential environment variables
Network request to external, non-affiliated domain

attack_chain.action: Attacker takes over abandoned package via expired maintainer domain (PyPI) or repo-jacking (Packagist).
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to publish malicious package versions.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is added to the package to steal AWS credentials from environment variables and exfiltrate them.
attack_chain.leads_to: Credential theft upon package installation or use.

attack_chain.action: Victim installs or updates the compromised package, triggering the malicious code.
attack_chain.leads_to: AWS credentials are sent to the attacker's Heroku endpoint.

attack_chain.action: Attacker receives AWS credentials, potentially enabling further compromise of victim infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: unauthorized access to AWS resources.

behavioral_signatures: Access to AWS_ACCESS_KEY and AWS_SECRET_KEY environment variables in third-party libraries
Unsolicited HTTP/HTTPS requests to external endpoints during package import or initialization
Network requests containing sensitive environment variable values
file_indicators: src/HauteLook/Phpass/PasswordHash.php with unexpected network or getenv code
Any code in dependency packages that reads AWS credentials and makes network requests
network_indicators: Unusual outbound HTTP requests to Herokuapp domains from build or runtime environments
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for third-party packages that access AWS credential environment variables and make outbound network requests, especially to untrusted domains. Use static analysis to flag getenv('AWS_ACCESS_KEY') or getenv('AWS_SECRET_KEY') combined with file_get_contents or curl to external URLs. Monitor network logs for requests to anti-theft-web.herokuapp.com or similar suspicious endpoints originating from build or CI/CD environments.
